name: Draft replies to Google reviews with Claude and approve them in Slack

parameters.content:
## Draft replies to Google reviews with Claude and approve them in Slack

Local businesses and franchises that answer reviews late, or only the bad ones.

### How it works
Trigger: Polls each platform's API or a review-aggregation provider hourly; negative reviews trigger immediate alerts.
1. Collect new reviews
2. Classify
3. Fetch context
4. Draft the response
5. Route negatives to a person first
6. Approve and post
7. Track resolution
8. Monthly insight report
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items; the write-back waits for an approval.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus Google Business Profile API / Birdeye / Podium, Slack / SMS.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Set your tone rules and the escalation words in the Config node; connect Birdeye or Podium if you aggregate reviews there.
Guardrail to keep: Negative and sensitive reviews are never answered publicly without a person's approval.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/review-response-automation/

## Trigger and config
The entry point and the one node you edit: names, approver, quiet hours, test mode.

## 1. Collect new reviews
Google Business Profile, Yelp, Trustpilot, Facebook, TripAdvisor and app stores, directly or via a provider such as Birdeye or Podium, per location

## 2. Classify
Sentiment, star rating context, topics (service, product, wait time, staff, pricing, cleanliness), and whether it mentions a specific staff member or a resolvable issue

## 3. Fetch context
For businesses with a CRM or booking system: the customer's visit or order, so the reply can reference it and a complaint can be checked against what happened

## 4. Draft the response
Positive: a specific thank-you that echoes what they praised, in the business voice, varied so replies never read as templated

## 5. Route negatives to a person first
Reviews below a rating threshold or mentioning safety, discrimination or legal issues go to the manager with the draft and the context; nothing is posted until they decide

nodes.name: Section: 5. Route negatives to a person first

parameters.content:
## 6. Approve and post
Drafts wait for one-click approval by the owner or location manager; approved replies post through the platform API

## 7. Track resolution
Negative reviews get a resolution status; follow-up reminders until closed; the reviewer's later rating change is recorded

## 8. Monthly insight report
Per location: rating trend, response rate and time, top praised and complained topics with examples, staff mentioned by name, and three operational suggestions drawn from the complaints

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Review platforms (Google, Yelp, Trustpilot, Facebook, app stores) or an aggregator
- CRM / booking / POS for customer context
- Business voice guide and response rules
- Location and manager directory

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Draft the response" step of the Review Response Automation workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Positive: a specific thank-you that echoes what they praised, in the business voice, varied so replies never read as templated. Negative: an empathetic acknowledgement, no defensiveness, an offer to resolve offline with a named contact.

Rules:
- Negative and sensitive reviews are never answered publicly without a person's approval.
- Replies never dispute facts in public, mention other customers, or reveal personal data.
- Positive-review auto-posting is enabled only after a calibration period and can be turned off per location.
- Platform rules (no incentives, no soliciting removal) are enforced in the response rules.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.
